parts.text: Drones in our fleet are of several models from different manufacturers, and they differ in how much they can carry, how far they can fly on a full battery, which sensors they carry, and which charging connector they use. Each drone has a home site, and we have a few dozen charging pads at our sites that use specific connector types which are not interchangeable. As a fleet technician, my tasks for day-to-day operations involve adding new drones, retiring old ones, setting up charging pads at our sites, taking drones out of service for repairs and putting them back, and sending drones to charge. Repairs and servicing are carried out by technicians, and regulators can ask a company to show how its drones have been looked after.
